metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 225. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.text: Chapter 1
brahmā devānāṃ prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptā
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> arose first among the gods, the maker of the universe and protector of the world.

children.text: sa brahmavidyāṃ sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhām atharvāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha ||
children.translated_text: He taught <s>Atharvan</s>, his eldest son, <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of brahman), the foundation of all knowledge.

children.text: atharvaṇe yāṃ pravadeta brahmā atharvā tāṃ purovācāṅgirase brahmavidyām
children.translated_text: That <s>brahmavidyā</s> which <s>Brahmā</s> declared to <s>Atharvan</s>, <s>Atharvan</s> formerly spoke to <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: sa bhāradvājāya satyavahāya prāha bhāradvājo 'ṅgirase parāvarām ||
children.translated_text: He taught it, the knowledge of both the higher and the lower, to <s>Satyavaha Bhāradvāja</s>; <s>Bhāradvāja</s> taught it to <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: śaunako ha vai mahāśālo 'ṅgirasaṃ vidhivad upasannaḥ papraccha
children.translated_text: <s>Śaunaka</s>, indeed a great householder, approached <s>Aṅgiras</s> according to rule and asked:

children.text: kasmin nu bhagavo vijñāte sarvam idaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: "By knowing what, venerable sir, does all this become known?"

children.text: tasmai sa hovāca
children.translated_text: To him he said:

children.text: dve vidye veditavya iti ha sma yad brahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca ||
children.translated_text: "Two kinds of knowledge are to be known, so indeed those who know brahman say: the higher and the lower.

children.text: tatrāparā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣam iti
children.translated_text: Of these, the lower is the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Atharvaveda, phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, meter, and astronomy.

children.text: atha parā yayā tad akṣaram adhigamyate ||
children.translated_text: But the higher is that by which the imperishable is attained.

children.text: yat tad adreśyam agrāhyam agotram avarṇam acakṣuḥśrotraṃ tad apāṇipādam
children.translated_text: That which is invisible, ungraspable, without lineage, without color, without eye or ear, without hand or foot,

children.text: nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ tad avyayaṃ yad bhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: eternal, all-pervading, present everywhere, exceedingly subtle, that imperishable source of beings the wise behold.

children.text: yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhṇate ca yathā pṛthivyām oṣadhayaḥ sambhavanti
children.translated_text: As a spider emits and draws back its thread, as plants arise upon the earth,

children.text: yathā sataḥ puruṣāt keśalomāni tathākṣarāt sambhavatīha viśvam ||
children.translated_text: and as hair and body-hair arise from a living person, so from the imperishable this universe arises here.

children.text: tapasā cīyate brahma tato 'nnam abhijāyate
children.translated_text: Through <s>tapas</s> (austerity, inner heat) brahman expands; from it food is born.

children.text: annāt prāṇo manaḥ satyaṃ lokāḥ karmasu cāmṛtam ||
children.translated_text: From food arise breath, mind, truth, the worlds, and immortality in ritual acts.

children.text: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: He who is all-knowing and all-wise, whose <s>tapas</s> consists of knowledge,

children.text: tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: from him this brahman, name, form, and food are born.

children.text: Chapter 2
tad etat satyam
children.translated_text: This indeed is the truth.

children.text: mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayo yānyapaśyaṃstāni tretāyāṃ bahudhā saṃtatāni
children.translated_text: The ritual acts which the seers saw in the mantras were widely extended in the Tretā age.

children.text: tāny ācaratha niyataṃ satyakāmā eṣa vaḥ panthāḥ sukṛtasya loke ||
children.translated_text: Perform them regularly, you who desire truth; this is your path in the world of merit.

children.text: yadā lelāyate hyarciḥ samiddhe havyavāhane
children.translated_text: When the flame flickers in the kindled carrier of oblations,

children.text: tadājyabhāgāvantareṇāhutīḥ pratipādayecchraddhayā hutam
children.translated_text: then, between the two portions of ghee, one should offer the oblations that are given with faith.

children.text: śraddhayā hutam om ||
children.translated_text: Offered with faith. Om.

children.text: yasyāgnihotram adarśam apaurṇamāsam acāturmāsyam anāgrayaṇam atithivarjitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Whose agnihotra is without the new-moon rite, without the full-moon rite, without the seasonal rites, without the first-fruits rite, and without hospitality to guests,

children.text: ahutam avaiśvadevam avidhinā hutam ā saptamāṃstasya lokān hinasti ||
children.translated_text: unoffered, without the Vaiśvadeva rite, or offered contrary to rule, it destroys his worlds up to the seventh.

children.text: kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Karālī</s>, <s>Manojavā</s>, <s>Sulohitā</s>, she who is smoke-colored,

children.text: sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sphuliṅginī</s>, and the goddess <s>Viśvarucī</s>: these, flickering, are the seven tongues of fire.

children.text: eteṣu yaś carate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālaṃ cāhutayo hyādadāyan
children.translated_text: Whoever acts among these shining flames, and offers oblations at the proper time,

children.text: taṃ nayantyetāḥ sūryasya raśmayo yatra devānāṃ patir eko 'dhivāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these rays of the sun lead him to where the one lord of the gods dwells.

children.text: ehy ehīti tam āhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ sūryasya raśmibhir yajamānaṃ vahanti
children.translated_text: "Come, come," the radiant oblations carry the sacrificer by the rays of the sun,

children.text: priyāṃ vācam abhivadantyo 'rcayantya eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmalokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: speaking pleasing words and honoring him: "This is your holy, well-earned world of brahman."

children.text: plavā hyete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ yeṣu karma
children.translated_text: For these raft-like forms of sacrifice are unsteady, the inferior work in which the eighteen are said to be involved.

children.text: etacchreyo ye 'bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punar evāpiyanti ||
children.translated_text: Fools who rejoice in this as the highest good go again to old age and death.

children.text: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ
children.translated_text: Dwelling in ignorance, considering themselves wise and learned,

children.text: jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fools wander about, being struck down, like blind men led by one who is blind.

children.text: avidyāyāṃ bahudhā vartamānā vayaṃ kṛtārthā ityabhimanyanti bālāḥ
children.translated_text: Living in ignorance in many ways, the immature think, "We have accomplished our aim."

children.text: yat karmiṇo na pravedayanti rāgāt tenāturāḥ kṣīṇalokāścyavante ||
children.translated_text: Because those devoted to works do not understand, through attachment, therefore, afflicted and with their worlds exhausted, they fall away.

children.text: iṣṭāpūrtaṃ manyamānā variṣṭhaṃ nānyacchreyo vedayante pramūḍhāḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking sacrifices and public works to be best, the deeply deluded know no other good.

children.text: nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte 'nubhūtvemaṃ lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśanti ||
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed their good deed on the back of heaven, they enter again this world, or one still lower.

children.text: tapaḥśraddhe ye hyupavasanty araṇye śāntā vidvāṃso bhaikṣacaryāṃ carantaḥ
children.translated_text: But those who dwell in the forest with <s>tapas</s> and faith, peaceful, learned, living on alms,

children.text: sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti yatrāmṛtaḥ sa puruṣo hyavyayātmā ||
children.translated_text: go stainless through the door of the sun, to where that immortal person, whose self is imperishable, abides.

children.text: parīkṣya lokān karmacitān brāhmaṇo nirvedam āyān nāsty akṛtaḥ kṛtena
children.translated_text: Having examined the worlds won by action, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should come to dispassion: what is unmade is not obtained by what is done.

children.text: tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurum evābhigacchet samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaṇiṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: In order to know that, he should approach only a teacher, with fuel in hand, one learned in scripture and established in brahman.

children.text: tasmai sa vidvān upasannāya samyak praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya
children.translated_text: To him, who has properly approached, whose mind is tranquil and who is endowed with calm, that wise teacher

children.text: yenākṣaraṃ puruṣaṃ veda satyaṃ provāca tāṃ tattvato brahmavidyām ||
children.translated_text: should teach in truth that <s>brahmavidyā</s> by which one knows the imperishable, true person.

children.text: Chapter 3
tad etat satyam
children.translated_text: This indeed is the truth.

children.text: yathā sudīptāt pāvakād visphuliṅgāḥ sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ
children.translated_text: As from a brightly blazing fire sparks of the same nature arise by the thousands,

children.text: tathākṣarād vividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ prajāyante tatra caivāpiyanti ||
children.translated_text: so, dear one, from the imperishable many kinds of beings are born, and into it indeed they return.

children.text: divyo hy amūrtaḥ puruṣo sa bāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ
children.translated_text: For the person is divine, formless, both outside and inside, and unborn.

children.text: aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhro hy akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is without breath, without mind, pure, and higher than the high imperishable.

children.text: etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca
children.translated_text: From this are born breath, mind, and all the senses,

children.text: khaṃ vāyur jyotir āpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: space, wind, fire, waters, and earth, the supporter of the universe.

children.text: agnir mūrdhā cakṣuṣī candrasūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāg vivṛtāśca vedāḥ
children.translated_text: Fire is his head; the moon and sun are his eyes; the directions are his ears; speech and the revealed Vedas are his mouth.

children.text: vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvam asya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hyeṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā ||
children.translated_text: Wind is his breath; the whole universe is his heart; from his feet is the earth, for he is the inner self of all beings.

children.text: tasmād agniḥ samidho yasya sūryaḥ somāt parjanya oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām
children.translated_text: From him comes fire, whose fuel is the sun; from the moon comes rain, and herbs upon the earth.

children.text: pumān retaḥ siñcati yoṣitāyāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣāt samprasūtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man pours seed into a woman; from the person many creatures are born.

children.text: tasmād ṛcaḥ sāma yajūṃṣi dīkṣā yajñāś ca sarve kratavo dakṣiṇāśca
children.translated_text: From him come the ṛc verses, the sāman chants, the yajus formulas, consecration, all sacrifices, rites, and priestly fees;

children.text: saṃvatsaraś ca yajamānaś ca lokāḥ somo yatra pavate yatra sūryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the year, the sacrificer, and the worlds where Soma is purified and where the sun shines.

children.text: tasmācca devā bahudhā samprasūtāḥ sādhyā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāṃsi
children.translated_text: From him too the gods are produced in many forms, the sādhyas, human beings, animals, and birds;

children.text: prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaś ca śraddhā satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidhiś ca ||
children.translated_text: breath and downward breath, rice and barley, austerity, faith, truth, chastity, and rule.

children.text: sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmāt saptārciṣaḥ samidhaḥ sapta homāḥ
children.translated_text: From him arise the seven vital breaths, the seven flames, the seven fuel-sticks, and the seven oblations;

children.text: sapta ime lokā yeṣu caranti prāṇā guhāśayā nihitāḥ sapta sapta ||
children.translated_text: and these seven worlds in which the breaths move, hidden in the cave, set down seven and seven.

children.text: ataḥ samudrā girayaś ca sarve 'smāt syandante sindhavaḥ sarvarūpāḥ
children.translated_text: From him come the oceans and all mountains; from him flow rivers of every form.

children.text: ataś ca sarvā oṣadhayo rasaś ca yenaiṣa bhūtais tiṣṭhate hy antarātmā ||
children.translated_text: From him come all plants and the sap by which this inner self stands among the elements.

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam
children.translated_text: The <s>puruṣa</s> alone is this whole universe: action, austerity, <s>brahman</s>, and the supreme immortal.

children.text: etad yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ so 'vidyāgranthiṃ vikiratīha somya ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows this, hidden in the cave, scatters here the knot of ignorance, dear one.

children.text: Chapter 4
āviḥ saṃnihitaṃ guhācaraṃ nāma mahat padam atraitat samarpitam
children.translated_text: Manifest, near at hand, moving in the cave, it is called the great abode; in it this is established.

children.text: ejat prāṇan nimiṣacca yad etajjānatha sadasadvareṇyam
children.translated_text: Whatever moves, breathes, and blinks, know that to be the excellent real and unreal,

children.text: paraṃ vijñānād yad variṣṭhaṃ prajānām ||
children.translated_text: that which is higher than knowledge and greatest among beings.

children.text: yad arcimad yad aṇubhyo 'ṇu ca yasmiṃllokā nihitā lokinaśca
children.translated_text: That which is radiant and subtler than the subtle, in which the worlds and the dwellers in the worlds are set,

children.text: tad etad akṣaraṃ brahma sa prāṇas tad u vāṅmanaḥ
children.translated_text: that is this imperishable <s>brahman</s>; that is breath; that indeed is speech and mind.

children.text: tad etat satyaṃ tad amṛtaṃ tadveddhavyaṃ somya viddhi ||
children.translated_text: That is truth; that is immortal. That is to be pierced, dear one: know it.

children.text: dhanurgṛhītvaupaniṣadaṃ mahāstraṃ śaraṃ hyupāsāniśitaṃ saṃdhayīta
children.translated_text: Taking up the Upaniṣadic bow, the great weapon, one should set upon it the arrow sharpened by meditation.

children.text: āyamya tad bhāvagatena cetasā lakṣyaṃ tad evākṣaraṃ somya viddhi ||
children.translated_text: Drawing it with a mind absorbed in that state, know, dear one, that very imperishable as the target.

children.text: praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hyātmā brahma tallakṣyam ucyate
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is the bow; the self is indeed the arrow; <s>brahman</s> is said to be its target.

children.text: apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravat tanmayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It is to be pierced without distraction; like an arrow, one should become one with it.

children.text: yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣam otaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiś ca sarvaiḥ
children.translated_text: Know that one self alone in whom heaven, earth, and the midspace are woven, together with the mind and all the breaths.

children.text: tam evaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam anyā vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let go of other words; this is the bridge to immortality.

children.text: arā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ sa eṣo 'ntaścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Where the channels are gathered together like spokes in the nave of a chariot-wheel, this one moves within, being born in many forms.

children.text: om ityevaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānaṃ svasti vaḥ pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt ||
children.translated_text: Meditate on the self simply as <s>oṃ</s>. May there be well-being for you in crossing beyond darkness.

children.text: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasyaiṣa mahimā bhuvi
children.translated_text: He who is all-knowing and all-wise, whose greatness is here on earth,

children.text: divye brahmapure hyeṣa vyomnyātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this self is established in the heavenly city of <s>brahman</s>, in the ether.

children.text: manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīranetā pratiṣṭhito 'nne hṛdayaṃ saṃnidhāya
children.translated_text: Made of mind, leader of the body and breath, established in food, placing himself close to the heart,

children.text: tad vijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrā ānandarūpam amṛtaṃ yad vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: the wise, through knowledge, behold that immortal one which shines forth as the form of bliss.

children.text: bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś chidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ
children.translated_text: The knot of the heart is split; all doubts are cut away;

children.text: kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare ||
children.translated_text: and his actions are exhausted when that which is both higher and lower is seen.

children.text: hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣkalam
children.translated_text: In the golden, supreme sheath is stainless, partless <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tacchubhraṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotistadyadātmavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is pure; it is the light of lights, which the knowers of the self know.

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ
children.translated_text: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine there, much less this fire.

children.text: tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: Everything shines after that alone as it shines; by its light all this shines forth.

children.text: brahmaivedam amṛtaṃ purastād brahma paścād brahma dakṣiṇataścottareṇa
children.translated_text: This immortal is <s>brahman</s> in front, <s>brahman</s> behind, <s>brahman</s> to the south and to the north;

children.text: adhaścordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvam idaṃ variṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: spread below and above, <s>brahman</s> alone is this whole universe, the highest.

children.text: Chapter 5
dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte
children.translated_text: Two fair-winged birds, joined companions and friends, embrace the same tree.

children.text: tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśīti ||
children.translated_text: Of the two, one eats the sweet fig; the other, not eating, merely looks on.

children.text: samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno 'nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: On the same tree the person, sunk down and deluded through helplessness, grieves.

children.text: juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśam asya mahimānamiti vītaśokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he sees the other, the beloved lord, and his greatness, then he becomes free from sorrow.

children.text: yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāram īśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim
children.translated_text: When the seer sees the golden-colored maker, the lord, the <s>puruṣa</s>, the source of <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: tadā vidvānpuṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti ||
children.translated_text: then, being wise, having shaken off merit and evil, stainless, he attains supreme equality.

children.text: prāṇo hyeṣa yaḥ sarvabhūtairvibhāti vijānan vidvān bhavate nātivādī
children.translated_text: For this is breath, which shines forth through all beings; knowing it, the wise man does not become one who speaks beyond measure.

children.text: ātmakrīḍa ātmaratiḥ kriyāvāneṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sporting in the self, delighting in the self, active in practice, he is the best of the knowers of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: satyena labhyastapasā hyeṣa ātmā samyagjñānena brahmacaryeṇa nityam
children.translated_text: This self is attained by truth, by austerity, by right knowledge, and always by chastity.

children.text: antaḥśarīre jyotirmayo hi śubhro yaṃ paśyanti yatayaḥ kṣīṇadoṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Within the body, luminous and pure, he is seen by ascetics whose faults have been exhausted.

children.text: satyam eva jayati nānṛtaṃ satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ
children.translated_text: Truth alone conquers, not falsehood; by truth the path of the gods is spread out,

children.text: yenākramantyṛṣayo hyāptakāmā yatra tat satyasya paramaṃ nidhānam ||
children.translated_text: by which the sages, their desires fulfilled, ascend to where that supreme treasure of truth is.

children.text: bṛhacca taddivyam acintyarūpaṃ sūkṣmācca tat sūkṣmataraṃ vibhāti
children.translated_text: That is great, heavenly, of inconceivable form; it shines subtler than the subtle.

children.text: dūrāt sudūre tad ihāntike ca paśyatsvihaiva nihitaṃ guhāyām ||
children.translated_text: It is farther than the far, and here it is near at hand, set right here in the cave among those who see.

children.text: na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā nānyairdevaistapasā karmaṇā vā
children.translated_text: It is not grasped by the eye, nor by speech, nor by other gods, nor by austerity or ritual action.

children.text: jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattvas tatastu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the serenity of knowledge, one whose being is purified then sees that partless one while meditating.

children.text: eṣo 'ṇurātmā cetasā veditavyo yasmin prāṇaḥ pañcadhā saṃviveśa
children.translated_text: This subtle self is to be known by the mind, in which breath has entered in fivefold form.

children.text: prāṇaiścittaṃ sarvam otaṃ prajānāṃ yasmin viśuddhe vibhavatyeṣa ātmā ||
children.translated_text: The whole mind of beings is woven with the breaths; when it is purified, this self shines forth in it.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ lokaṃ manasā saṃvibhāti viśuddhasattvaḥ kāmayate yāṃśca kāmān
children.translated_text: Whatever world the purified one, whose being is clear, imagines with his mind, and whatever desires he desires,

children.text: taṃ taṃ lokaṃ jayate tāṃśca kāmāṃs tasmād ātmajñaṃ hyarcayed bhūtikāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that world he wins, and those desires too. Therefore one who desires prosperity should honor the knower of the self.

children.text: Chapter 6
sa vedaitat paramaṃ brahma dhāma yatra viśvaṃ nihitaṃ bhāti śubhram
children.translated_text: He knows this supreme abode of <s>brahman</s>, where the universe is set and shines, pure.

children.text: upāsate puruṣaṃ ye hyakāmās te śukram etad ativartanti dhīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those who, being without desires, worship the <s>puruṣa</s>, those steadfast ones pass beyond this seed of generation.

children.text: kāmān yaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ sa kāmabhir jāyate tatra tatra
children.translated_text: Whoever desires objects of desire, thinking upon them, is born here and there through those desires.

children.text: paryāptakāmasya kṛtātmanastvihaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for one whose desires are fulfilled, whose self has been perfected, all desires dissolve here itself.

children.text: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena
children.translated_text: This <s>ātman</s> is not to be attained by instruction, nor by intelligence, nor by much hearing.

children.text: yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām ||
children.translated_text: It is attained by the one whom this very <s>ātman</s> chooses; to him this <s>ātman</s> reveals its own form.

children.text: nāyam ātmā balahīnena labhyo na ca pramādāt tapaso vāpyaliṅgāt
children.translated_text: This <s>ātman</s> is not to be attained by one without strength, nor through heedlessness, nor by austerity devoid of the proper marks.

children.text: etairupāyairyatate yastu vidvāṃs tasyaiṣa ātmā viśate brahma dhāma ||
children.translated_text: But the wise man who strives by these means: into him this <s>ātman</s> enters as the abode of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: samprāpyainam ṛṣayo jñānatṛptāḥ kṛtātmāno vītarāgāḥ praśāntāḥ
children.translated_text: Having attained this, the seers, satisfied by knowledge, perfected in self, free from passion, and tranquil,

children.text: te sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrā yuktātmānaḥ sarvam evāviśanti ||
children.translated_text: those steadfast ones, having reached the all-pervading one everywhere, with selves disciplined, enter into everything itself.

children.text: vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogādyatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ
children.translated_text: The ascetics whose understanding of the Vedānta is firmly ascertained, whose being is purified through the yoga of renunciation,

children.text: te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve ||
children.translated_text: all of them, at the final end, in the worlds of <s>brahman</s>, being supremely immortal, are completely released.

children.text: gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhā devāśca sarve pratidevatāsu
children.translated_text: The fifteen parts have gone to their foundations, and all the deities to their corresponding deities;

children.text: karmāṇi vijñānamayaśca ātmā pare 'vyaye sarva ekībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: actions, and the self consisting of knowledge, all become one in the supreme imperishable.

children.text: yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre 'staṃ gacchanti nāmarūpe vihāya
children.translated_text: As flowing rivers disappear in the ocean, abandoning name and form,

children.text: tathā vidvān nāmarūpādvimuktaḥ parāt paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam ||
children.translated_text: so the knower, freed from name and form, reaches the divine <s>puruṣa</s>, higher than the high.

children.text: sa yo ha vai tatparamaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati nāsyābrahmavit kule bhavati
children.translated_text: He who indeed knows that supreme <s>brahman</s> becomes <s>brahman</s> itself; in his family there is no one who does not know <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tarati śokaṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ guhāgranthibhyo vimukto 'mṛto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He crosses beyond sorrow, he crosses beyond evil; freed from the knots of the heart-cave, he becomes immortal.

children.text: tad etad ṛcābhyuktam ||
children.translated_text: This has been declared by a verse.

children.text: kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ juhvata ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who perform the rites, who are learned in the Veda, steadfast in <s>brahman</s>, who themselves offer the single-seer fire with faith,

children.text: teṣām evaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta śirovrataṃ vidhivadyaistu cīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: to them alone one should teach this brahmavidyā, to those by whom the head-vow has been duly observed.

children.text: tad etat satyam ṛṣiraṅgirāḥ purovāca naitad acīrṇavrato 'dhīte namaḥ paramarṣibhyo namaḥ paramarṣibhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is true. The seer <s>Aṅgiras</s> spoke it formerly. One who has not observed the vow does not study this. Homage to the supreme seers; homage to the supreme seers.
